subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The city of Gracklstugh is a plain, functional work camp where buildings lack art, walls are unadorned, and the air is thick with acrid smoke from forges and smelters, making breathing difficult and burning the sense of smell.
source_quote: The buildings are plain and functional. Whereas the Drow would have decorated their homes with etchings and art, the walls of the Duergar homes are plain. And the ambiance is just that of work. The sound of hammers warping metals, the stench and heat, and the light of the smelters make all of Gracklstugh appear as one large work camp. But the acrid smoke makes breathing hard and burns through his sense of smell, which he will remember most from his time here.

subject: Blade Bazaar
fact: The Blade Bazaar is a marketplace named after the most abundant goods the Duergar offer, where shops sell almost everything available in the city, alongside stalls by visiting merchants, and the din of people arguing in Dwarvish nearly drowns out the hammering from the city’s forges, offering a good chance to slip away from pursuers.
source_quote: This marketplace is named after the most abundant goods the duergar offer, but the shops here sell almost everything available in the city, along with stalls set up by visiting merchants. The din of people arguing, mainly in Dwarvish, nearly drowns out the hammering coming from the city’s forges, and the crowds here offer a good chance to slip away from pursuers.

subject: The Tongue of Madness
fact: The Tongue of Madness is a magical mushroom that, when eaten, compels the consumer to speak their truest thoughts and hidden opinions aloud, revealing secrets and personal judgments.
source_quote: Zalthir hands him a mushroom, The Tongue of Madness, and says, "Eat." And Buppido does and starts talking. "I just wanted to return to my bolt hole in the caverns near the city and praise the Divine Plan." And then he starts expressing his true opinions of his companions: "You all have been so annoying. Daz has foul-smelling breath. Thorin thinks his muscles are impressive. Eldeth is -not- interested in him."

subject: Jug of Any Liquid
fact: A jug found in the Duergar keelboat that can generate any liquid, and when first used, produces mayonnaise, which enhances the taste of bland food like mushrooms.
source_quote: He finds some gold and a jug that he learns later can be used to generate any liquid. The first liquid they generate is mayonnaise. After eating bland mushrooms, mayonnaise will make anything taste much better.

subject: Duergar Keelboat
fact: A boat identified by the Duergar as their own, containing crates and later revealed to be abandoned, used as a vessel by the Duergar for transport and possibly slave trafficking.
source_quote: Yes, it’s Duergar Keelboat. You can see the crates.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido is a repentant Duergar who claims his actions were guided by the Divine Plan, later exposed as lying and manipulative after consuming the Tongue of Madness, revealing contempt for his companions and delusional self-justification.
source_quote: Look, I made mistakes. It was the divine plan. Just let me go. I won’t bother you again.” ... "I just wanted to return to my bolt hole in the caverns near the city and praise the Divine Plan." ... "You all have been so annoying. Daz has foul-smelling breath. Thorin thinks his muscles are impressive. Eldeth is -not- interested in him."

subject: Dulgir
fact: Dulgir is a Duergar merchant at the Blade Bazaar who initially curses Grygum but shifts speech patterns to a Baldurian patriar tone during negotiation, and later denies the existence of an invisible brother, contributing to the perception of widespread madness in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The Duergar starts cursing Grygum... speaks with the stilted tongue of a Baldurian patriar... "His brother doesn’t exist."

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a gnome who corrects Zalthir’s misunderstanding of planar magic, explaining that summoning deities like Demogorgon requires powerful artifacts and rituals, and who later mocks Grygum’s complaints about his bEttin g, revealing a sharp, irreverent personality.
source_quote: Obviously, you do not understand the first thing about interplanar or gate travel... The great powers of the outer planes in the Time of Trouble could enter the Prime Material Plane at will... No, Buppido has no such powers... GIVE IT A REST.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc cleric of Bahamut who observes the political and psychological undercurrents of Duergar society, concluding that conflict stems from resource competition, not divine will, and who notes the city’s madness with growing unease.
source_quote: This is not the will of any god. This is the will of the people... I am convinced that some madness afflicts the city, perhaps the same madness that consumed the Kuotoans.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn who uses magic to manipulate darkness and water, negotiates for magical items like the Eldritch Claw Tattoo, and becomes increasingly frustrated by the chaos and unpredictability of his companions and the city’s madness.
source_quote: I sense some racial animus... I like him... Can he summon Demogorgon like the Kuo-toans?... I found this list of names earlier... They could be people who could help us.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a warrior who alternates between brute intimidation and reluctant diplomacy, wields a sword and crossbow, and is deeply affected by the revelations of the Tongue of Madness and the instability of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: And just so we are clear, if we don’t get what we want, and you betray us, there will be consequences... I lower my weapon, uncertain... Thorin decides he’s heard enough... Thorin approaches the boat and notices that Eldeth is not one of those captured.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a spellcaster who specializes in area-of-effect magic, including magic missile and shape water, and is repeatedly frustrated by the timing and consequences of his own spells, yet remains optimistic and practical.
source_quote: The magic missile will do just fine here... "I have shape water!"... The darkness is annoying... I will need area-of-effect spells.

subject: The Two-Headed Giant’s Breakthrough
fact: A two-headed, gray-skinned giant bursts through a gate in Gracklstugh, howling madly, smashing stone and debris, and killing a Duergar soldier whose broken body flies through the air and crashes nearby, triggering panic and marking a turning point in the city’s descent into chaos.
source_quote: A two-headed, gray-skinned giant burst through a gate, howling madly and lashing out left and right, littering the plaza with rock and stone debris. As he bellows, one of his swings connects with a duergar soldier, whose broken body flies through the air and crashes near you with a sickening crunch.

subject: The Tongue of Madness Revelation
fact: Buppido consumes the Tongue of Madness and speaks aloud hidden truths about his companions, exposing their flaws, romantic tensions, and personal grievances, leading Thorin to abandon his plan to kill him and Grygum to declare he has heard enough.
source_quote: And Buppido does and starts talking... "You all have been so annoying. Daz has foul-smelling breath. Thorin thinks his muscles are impressive. Eldeth is -not- interested in him."... "Zalthir’s scales haven’t been cleaned in ages."... "Jimjar’s bEttin g is so annoying! GIVE IT A REST."

subject: The Invisible Brother Incident
fact: At the Blade Bazaar, a cloth merchant suddenly stops negotiating and speaks to an invisible brother, who Dulgir insists does not exist, reinforcing the perception that madness is pervasive and reality is unstable in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The merchant suddenly stops mid-negotiating and starts talking to someone he refers to as his brother... "My brother!"... "His brother doesn’t exist."

subject: The Duergar Keelboat Encounter
fact: The party discovers an abandoned Duergar keelboat containing crates, later revealing hidden Duergar activity, leading to a confrontation where Daz’s shape water spell exposes an invisible Duergar, Zalthir uses darkness to attack, and multiple Duergar are killed in rapid succession.
source_quote: Yes, it’s Duergar Keelboat. You can see the crates... I have shape water!... water is sprayed around the boat, and the outline of a humanoid appears... Zalthir invokes Darkness and plunges into the water to attack the foe... Another belch sounds, and another Duergar dies covered in acid.

subject: Darklake District
fact: The Darklake District is the only area in Gracklstugh where non-Duergars are permitted to move freely, separated from the rest of the city by gates, and appears calm compared to the chaotic, mad interior, yet still infected by the city’s underlying instability.
source_quote: Non-Duergars are only permitted to move freely in the Darklake district... The gates at the end of the road keep the Darklake District isolated from the rest of the city. It looks calm.

subject: Two-Headed Gray-Skinned Giant
fact: A two-headed, gray-skinned giant that bursts through a gate in Gracklstugh, howling madly and killing a Duergar soldier with a single blow, representing an eruption of uncontrollable chaos within the city’s rigid order.
source_quote: A two-headed, gray-skinned giant burst through a gate, howling madly and lashing out left and right... one of his swings connects with a duergar soldier, whose broken body flies through the air and crashes near you with a sickening crunch.

subject: Invisible Duergar
fact: Duergar warriors who can become invisible at will, often ambush opponents and deny their presence even when observed, contributing to the paranoia and instability of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The Duergar can become invisible at will; you never know who is watching... The Duergar can become invisible for a whole hour... Hemeth... turns invisible... "I will be hiding here."
